clue.text: Obstructionist's contribution to wheelwright's product?

parts.note: an obstructive person is said to put one of these rods into somebody's wheel, and a wheelwright fits them between hub and rim

explanation.surface: A question about what a troublemaker adds to a cartwheel-maker's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'put a spoke in someone's wheel' means to hinder their plans, so the obstructionist's contribution to a wheel is literally one of its rods.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for thwarting a plan is to put one of these wheel rods into someone's wheel, so it is the obstructer's contribution.

clue.text: Flay the old pirate Scrooge

parts.note: to flay is to strip off the hide, to skin
Captain Flint is the old pirate of Treasure Island, whose parrot repeats his name

explanation.surface: An instruction to whip the miserly old pirate Scrooge.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge is the miser of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, used here as a common noun for any miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge is the archetypal tight-fisted man, and a tightwad is exactly that.

clue.text: Sebastian Melmoth shows no mark of battle

parts.note: O, a nought, stands for nothing or no
a scar is a mark left by a wound, as from battle

explanation.surface: A man named Sebastian Melmoth bears no wounds from fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Melmoth was the name Oscar Wilde lived under in exile in France after prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde adopted the alias Sebastian Melmoth in his last years, so the alias stands for his first name.

clue.text: Repayment incomplete for redesign of highest heaven

indicators.note: a redesign reworks the shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
incomplete says the word Repayment loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A partial repayment pays for remodelling the loftiest paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts REPAYMENT to REPAYMEN, and 'redesign of' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In old cosmology the empyrean was the outermost sphere, the abode of God and the uppermost of the heavens.

clue.text: Would-be husband holds place on retirement as a journalist

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: a suitor is a man courting a woman he hopes to marry
on retiring for the night one goes to bed

explanation.surface: A man hoping to marry keeps his job after retirement as a newspaperman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub-editor is a newspaper staffer who checks and corrects copy before it is printed.

clue.text: Discarded lower-class accommodation?

definitions.meaning: cast off, as a snake its skin or a tree its leaves
a humble garden hut, jokingly housing for the lowly

explanation.surface: Rejected housing for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off, and a shed is a lowly outbuilding, a humorous lodging for those of low class.

clue.text: As abysmal as Pyramus and Thisby without Pyramus

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the weaver Bottom plays Pyramus in the play of Pyramus and Thisby
less means without, as in hopeless

explanation.surface: A verdict that the rustics' play is dreadful, and would be worse without its hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the actor of Pyramus from the play and it is Bottom-less; abysmal in its old sense means fathomless.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal originally meant like an abyss, unfathomably deep, which is having no floor.

clue.text: To play the dilettante looks very black in the depression

indicators.note: in places the very black letters within the word for a valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley, a depression in the land
BB marks a very soft, very black pencil lead

explanation.surface: An amateur's dabbling looks gloomy amid his depression.
explanation.walkthrough: BB is the pencil grade for a very black lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To dabble is to take up a pursuit superficially, as an amateur does.

clue.text: Paper shows old Hebrew image without nether limb

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the image goes round the limb

parts.note: a teraph is an idol or household god of the ancient Hebrews
the leg is the lower limb

explanation.surface: A newspaper prints a picture of an ancient Hebrew idol missing its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense 'outside', which is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper.

clue.text: Beam in operation, making material.

parts.note: a beam of light is a ray
a machine in operation is on

explanation.surface: A beam of light at work produces a textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fabric made from cellulose.

clue.text: Beginning inspection — not so unusual after one

indicators.note: the rearranged inspection comes after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: unusual signals the remaining letters are rearranged
not so tells us to take the letters S and O out of the word inspection

explanation.surface: Starting an inspection that, after the first, is less out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' deletes two letters from the inspection, and 'unusual' rearranges the eight left (INPECTIN) to follow the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipient describes something in its first stages, just starting.

clue.text: Excellent beef

definitions.meaning: an old exclamation of approval, splendid
corned beef, as in the canned army ration

explanation.surface: Praise for fine meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bully! is dated slang for splendid, and bully beef is tinned corned meat.

clue.text: Warning of course about the old city causes wild excitement

indicators.note: about here means around, so the warning surrounds the city

parts.note: golfers on a course shout fore as a warning
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A warning about the ancient city stirs up frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course, where FORE is shouted.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public excitement or uproar.

clue.text: Possible gain after school expels to wit this ruffian

indicators.note: the rearranged gain follows the shortened school
school expelling something means those letters are thrown out of the word

parts.note: sc., short for scilicet, means to wit

indicators.note: possible marks one of the possible rearrangements of the word gain

explanation.surface: A school throwing out a lout might improve things.
explanation.walkthrough: sc. (scilicet, Latin 'namely') is the dictionary abbreviation for 'to wit'; 'expels' removes it, and 'Possible' scrambles the gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is a violent young troublemaker, a rowdy thug.

clue.text: Have to support eg custard pie: as facial application

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower word supports the upper one

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, of which a custard pie is an example

explanation.surface: A slapstick custard pie as something to put on the face.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for pudding; HAVE goes beneath it in this down answer. The surface suggests a custard pie in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a lotion a man puts on his face after shaving.

clue.text: Brave way Wenceslas and his page finished their journey

definitions.text: Brave way Wenceslas and his page finished their journey

parts.words: Brave way Wenceslas and his page finished their journey
parts.note: a Native American brave walks in single file, and the carol's page trod in his master's footsteps

explanation.surface: How the good king and his servant finished trudging through the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol Good King Wenceslas, the page treads in the king's footprints, one behind the other; a brave is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian file is single file, people walking one behind another.

clue.text: 100 tales of French romance perhaps

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of romance may be another arrangement

explanation.surface: A hundred stories of a French love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' looks like the genre of the tales, but it is only letters for 'perhaps' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a collection of a hundred stories told over ten days.

clue.text: Insect was quietly beginning to worry a snake

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A bug quietly began bothering a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers a second route too: W, the first letter of 'worry', plus ASP, a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is a stinging winged insect.

clue.text: Flower on tap? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in a down answer the flower sits on top of the tap

parts.note: the poppy is a red flower
a cock is a tap or valve

explanation.surface: A flower growing on a tap, met with scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppycock is dismissive slang for rubbish talk.

clue.text: In mint condition, as Ibsen's hero was said to be aware

parts.note: Brand is the hero of Ibsen's verse play of that name

indicators.note: said to be signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: to be aware, in the past, is to have known: knew

explanation.surface: Ibsen's hero was reportedly fresh and aware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was aware' means KNEW, heard as NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand-new means completely new and unused, as a coin fresh from the mint.

clue.text: Drum-beat summoning W. G. Bunter?

definitions.meaning: a beat of the drum, an old Scottish term
food, the schoolboy treat that would call the greedy Billy Bunter

explanation.surface: A drum roll calling the fat schoolboy to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy (William George) Bunter is the greedy fat boy of the Greyfriars school stories, obsessed with tuck, British school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck of drum is an old Scots phrase for a drumbeat, and tuck is schoolboy slang for sweets and cakes.

clue.text: Spice shorn perhaps from film by this

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Racy bits are cut from a film by the censor's scissors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SPICE SHORN; spice here means racy content.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorship cuts objectionable material out of films and books.

clue.text: United States do it wrong in scene of shooting

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are put together incorrectly

explanation.surface: Americans get it wrong at the place where filming happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' is filming, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A film studio is where movies are shot.

clue.text: Like Wardle's fat boy, come to eat cooked oats

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside
cooked tells us the letters of oats are mixed

explanation.surface: Dickens's sleepy fat boy being called to eat porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe, Mr Wardle's fat boy in The Pickwick Papers, is always falling asleep. 'cooked' makes ATOS from OATS, which COME eats.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy is perpetually dozing, which is a state of deep unconsciousness.

clue.text: Tummy trouble requires oil mixture in small quantity

indicators.note: in places the mixed oil inside the small quantity

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetre, is a small measure

indicators.note: a mixture of the letters of oil is wanted

explanation.surface: A stomach complaint calls for an oily medicine in a small dose.
explanation.walkthrough: cc (cubic centimetre) is a small dose of medicine; 'mixture' doubles as the pharmacy word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is acute abdominal pain, especially in babies.

clue.text: Point to baby's wear that's neat and elegant

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a nappy is the British word for a diaper

explanation.surface: Pointing to a baby's tidy and smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPY is British for diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean smart and stylish, as in a snappy dresser.

clue.text: Balance shown by first of paddlers on French river

indicators.note: in a down answer the letter sits on top of the river
first of picks out the opening letter of paddlers

parts.note: the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: Canoeists on a French river show steadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is steadiness and equilibrium.

clue.text: Notices, say, a tool

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the word

parts.note: ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: Notices, for example, about a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to its handle.

clue.text: We hear you are seen in a hat of ghastly hue

indicators.note: seen in places the heard letters inside the hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: we hear marks a sound-alike

parts.note: the phrase spoken sounds like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: You are told to appear in a hat of sickly colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you are' spoken sounds like UR; LID is slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid once meant pale and sallow, of a ghastly, sickly colour.

clue.text: Movement in notes and a refusal to accept metal money

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the refusal goes round the money

parts.note: no is a refusal
tin is slang for money, and also a metal

explanation.surface: A piece of music, and someone refusing to take coins.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking and a piece played in that tempo, slightly faster than andante.

clue.text: One instance perhaps of an eastern language?

definitions.text: One instance perhaps of an eastern language?

parts.words: One instance perhaps of an eastern language?
parts.note: Chinese has several spoken varieties, so this is one example of a far eastern tongue

explanation.surface: A question asking for an example of an oriental tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that this is a loose description: one spoken variety of Chinese, centred on Guangzhou and Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: The dialect of Guangzhou and Hong Kong is one of the major varieties of Chinese.

clue.text: Bring about a noisome effluvium, say

indicators.note: say indicates a word spoken aloud

parts.note: a reek is a foul smell

explanation.surface: Causing a nasty smell, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreak havoc is to cause or inflict it.
